name: SIGMA - Suricata ZK-LAB login burst
description: Network-side view of the same attack. Suricata rule 9000001 fired (20+ POSTs to /login/ from one source in 60 s), so the SIEM sees it even if the application logs are lost.
author: Darius Onofrei
false_positives: Load tests against the auth service
query: from logs-suricata-* metadata _id, _index, _version | where event.kind=="alert" and rule.id==9000001

name: SIGMA - zk-auth brute force from one source
description: Ten or more failed logins from the same source IP within five minutes (password guessing or credential stuffing).
author: Darius Onofrei
false_positives: Several users behind one NAT mistyping passwords
query:
from logs-zkauth-* metadata _id, _index, _version | where (event.action in ("login-password", "login-zk")) and event.outcome=="failure"
| eval timebucket=date_trunc(5minutes, @timestamp) | stats event_count=count() by timebucket, source.ip
| where event_count >= 10

name: SIGMA - zk-auth forged Schnorr proof
description: A zero-knowledge login with a fresh nonce failed verification. The prover does not know the secret key for the registered public key (forgery or wrong key).
author: Darius Onofrei
false_positives: A user whose client lost or rotated its key
query: from logs-zkauth-* metadata _id, _index, _version | where event.action=="login-zk" and event.outcome=="failure" and event.reason=="invalid_proof"

name: SIGMA - zk-auth Schnorr proof replay
description: A zero-knowledge login reused a server nonce that was already consumed. An honest client never does this; it means a captured proof is being replayed.
author: Darius Onofrei
false_positives: A client bug that retries the same request after a timeout
query: from logs-zkauth-* metadata _id, _index, _version | where event.action=="login-zk" and event.outcome=="failure" and event.reason=="nonce_reuse"
